title: From the sign-flip diagnostic to reaching the interior
content: The abstract path-following engine SpernerTuckerPathFollowing.exists_interior_degree_one turns an EVEN total number of degree-1 endpoints (handshaking) and an ODD number of BOUNDARY degree-1 endpoints into a degree-1 endpoint that is INTERIOR — the Tucker witness. Its first concrete instantiation (SpernerTuckerHexagonSignFlipEngine) fired the engine on the UNDIRECTED sign-flip door graph and produced only a diagnostic: the endpoint always lands on an antipodal-boundary edge of the opposite hemisphere, never interior, because that graph is all cycles with no interior endpoints. A complete finite classification of all 2^16 undirected edge-local rules proved WHY (no undirected rule can carry an odd full-circle seed) and singled out the ORIENTED directed pos→neg sign rule door(x→y) ⇔ sgn x = 0 ∧ sgn y = 1 as the essentially-unique closer, whose two abstract blades were verified in the sibling oq-07. This file runs those blades through the engine's parity split ON THE DISC ROOMS and reaches the conclusion the sign-flip engine could not: an odd — hence non-zero — number of degree-1 rooms whose single door is INTERIOR.
mathContext: The engine's handshaking lemma: in a graph of maximum degree ≤ 2 (paths and cycles) the number of degree-1 vertices is even; splitting them by a boundary predicate, an odd boundary part forces an odd, hence non-empty, interior part. Here the 'vertices' are the six disc rooms T_i = (centre, v_i, v_{i+1}) and 'degree-1' means the room carries exactly one directed door.

title: The antipodal labelling model and the directed door indicator
content: negL = ![2,3,0,1] is label negation on {+1,+2,−1,−2} (Fin 4). V a b c = ![a,b,c,negL a,negL b,negL c] gives the six boundary labels from three free labels a,b,c on v₀,v₁,v₂ with the antipodal condition v_{i+3} = −v_i built in. rot i = i+1 is the cyclic successor. sgn = ![0,0,1,1] is the sign map {+1,+2}↦0, {−1,−2}↦1. dir x y := if x = 0 ∧ y = 1 then 1 else 0 is the directed pos→neg door indicator on ZMod 2 sign bits: an oriented sign edge is a door iff it runs from a +-sign vertex (0) to a −-sign vertex (1). This is the identical encoding to the sibling SpernerTuckerHexagonDirectedSignDoor (oq-07).
mathContext: Boundary vertices v₀,…,v₅ of the hexagon S¹ with v_{i+3} = −v_i (a free antipodal action i ↦ i+3 on Fin 6), plus one interior centre vertex with free label d. The sign map is antipodal: sgn(negL x) = sgn x + 1, which is why the antipode reverses a directed door 0→1 into a non-door 1→0.

title: Rooms of the disc: interior and boundary directed doors
content: Each triangle T_i = (centre d, v_i, v_{i+1}) is a room oriented d→v_i→v_{i+1}→d, with three oriented sides split into two INTERIOR spokes (d→v_i, v_{i+1}→d) and one BOUNDARY edge (v_i→v_{i+1}). intDoor a b c d i := dir (sgn d) (sgn (V a b c i)) + dir (sgn (V a b c (rot i))) (sgn d) counts the directed doors on the two interior spokes; bdDoor a b c d i := dir (sgn (V a b c i)) (sgn (V a b c (rot i))) counts the boundary edge; roomDoor := intDoor + bdDoor is the total over all three sides, equal to SpernerTuckerHexagonDirectedSignDoor.hexDirTri. room_door_le_one proves every room has ≤ 1 directed door — so a degree-1 room's single door is interior XOR boundary, never both.
mathContext: roomDoor ≤ 1 is the path-structure blade of oq-07 (hexagon_dirTri_le_one): an oriented triangle of sign bits has at most one 0→1 edge. It makes the disc door graph a union of paths (degree-1 endpoints) rather than the all-cycles undirected sign-flip graph, and it makes the interior/boundary split of a degree-1 room exclusive.

title: The three degree-1 room counts
content: interiorDeg1 a b c d := #{i : Fin 6 | roomDoor a b c d i = 1 ∧ intDoor a b c d i = 1} counts the degree-1 rooms whose single door is on an interior spoke; boundaryDeg1 counts those whose door is on the boundary edge (roomDoor = 1 ∧ bdDoor = 1); totalDeg1 counts all degree-1 rooms (roomDoor = 1). These Finset cardinalities are the concrete-room analogues of the abstract engine's interior-endpoint, boundary-endpoint and total-endpoint counts, all with decidable predicates over the finite room index Fin 6.
mathContext: In the Freund–Todd picture these count, respectively, the path endpoints that are genuine interior pivot-terminal rooms, the endpoints forced on the antipodal boundary by the odd seed, and all path endpoints. The handshaking lemma relates the three.

title: Handshaking and the odd boundary seed (the two engine hypotheses)
content: total_deg1_even proves the total number of degree-1 rooms is EVEN (values ∈ {4,6} over all 256 antipodal labellings) — the concrete-room form of the engine's handshaking lemma even_card_degree_one. boundary_deg1_odd proves the number of BOUNDARY degree-1 rooms is ODD (values ∈ {1,3}) — the odd boundary seed, the room count of the odd full-circle directed door count full_dir_count_odd from oq-07. handshake_split proves total = interior + boundary, the exclusive interior/boundary split of degree-1 rooms (valid because roomDoor ≤ 1). All three are decided by the kernel over the finite labelling space.
mathContext: These are precisely the two hypotheses of SpernerTuckerPathFollowing.exists_interior_degree_one (even total endpoints; odd boundary endpoints), plus the split identity that makes the parity subtraction meaningful. Orientation is what makes the boundary count odd: the undirected sign-flip rule has an even boundary count because the antipodal involution pairs its doors, while the directed rule's antipode reverses its doors (oq-07 dir_antipode_reverse).

title: The payoff: an odd, positive number of interior degree-1 rooms
content: interior_deg1_odd derives — by pure parity, NOT re-enumeration — that the number of INTERIOR degree-1 rooms is ODD: rewrite total_deg1_even to (total even) and boundary_deg1_odd to (boundary odd), substitute handshake_split (total = interior + boundary), and omega forces interior odd. This is the exact mechanism of exists_interior_degree_one (even endpoints, odd boundary ⇒ odd interior), here forcing a POSITIVE interior endpoint count. interior_deg1_eq_three sharpens it to exactly 3; interior_deg1_pos gives positivity (odd ⇒ ≥ 1); and exists_interior_room extracts the witness room FROM the parity count via Finset.card_pos — the concrete realization of the engine with a genuine interior endpoint, precisely what SpernerTuckerHexagonSignFlipEngine (interior count 0) could not produce.
mathContext: even − odd = odd is the whole content: the handshaking-even total minus the odd boundary seed leaves an odd, hence non-zero, interior count. exists_interior_room mirrors the abstract engine's own proof, which also extracts its interior endpoint from Finset.card_pos on a positive count. Honest scope: an interior degree-1 room is the Freund–Todd pivot's terminal room; its interior directed door is a genuine complementary edge (λ u = −λ v) only half the time, so identifying it with the Tucker witness still needs pivot-connectivity.
